title: Sparse Matrix Multiplication
hints: Most entries of both matrices are zero, and a zero contributes nothing to any product term. Think about which multiplications the standard triple loop performs that can never matter.
Instead of computing each output cell as a dot product of a row and a column, consider what a single non-zero entry mat1[i][k] contributes to the output, and which entries of mat2 it pairs with.

All the cost of the triple loop sits in the shared inner dimension. Organize the work around that shared index, so that a non-zero of mat1 only ever meets the non-zeros of mat2 it can actually pair with.
